bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt to Equity (x) charted as 0.39 (FY24), 0.52 (FY25), 0.66 (FY26) - i.e. rising over the three years shown.
- Net Worth (INR Mn) charted as 11,238 (FY24), 12,127 (FY25), 12,283 (FY26); Total Equity in the balance sheet matches at 11,238 / 12,127 / 12,283.
- Balance sheet shows Capital work-in-progress rising 415 (FY24) to 1,552 (FY25) to 2,625 (FY26) INR Mn, alongside Property, plant and equipment of 14,678 / 16,013 / 18,099 INR Mn - reinvestment in the mill upgrade.
- Non-current Borrowings rose 3,070 (FY24) to 4,027 (FY25) to 5,897 (FY26) INR Mn; current Borrowings 2,055 / 2,509 / 2,701 INR Mn.
- Cash Conversion Cycle charted as 56 (FY24), 92 (FY25), 75 (FY26). The deck discloses no dividend policy or payout.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Fully backward-integrated operations (agro & wood pulping, co-generation power, chemical recovery) giving control over the value chain and cost structure
- Diversified product portfolio across Maplitho, Copier, Creamwove and Specialty papers, including sustainable single-use-plastic replacement grades
- Established pan-India distribution via 120+ dealers plus a growing global export footprint (26 countries)
- AI/digital-led operational efficiency through Project Nirmaan and Project Neev (dataPARC, KPI dashboards, Advanced Process Control)
- Social Farm Forestry programme (nearly 18,300+ acres, 19,100+ farmers) securing long-term wood raw-material supply
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material supply risk (wood/agro residue) — Seasonal availability of agro residue and surging demand for wood from other wood-based industries (MDF/Ply/Peeling/Particle Board) can cause supply shortages and escalate prices; mitigated via farmer tie-ups, in-house pulping and backward integration.
- Import competition — Cost-effective paper imports from ASEAN and East Asia (particularly China and Indonesia) have contributed to a 10-15% drop in domestic prices in recent months, pressuring sales and margins for Indian producers including Kuantum.
- Raw material and finished-goods price volatility — Fluctuations in pulp, bamboo and imported material prices can significantly impact profit margins; the Company relies on smart pricing strategies and partial backward integration to limit the impact.
- Digital substitution — Growing adoption of digital learning, cloud communication and e-governance is gradually eroding demand for traditional printing and writing paper, a core segment for the Company.
- Energy dependence and rising power costs — Rising power costs and fossil-fuel dependence can impact operational efficiency and raise expenses; mitigated by the Company's in-house co-generation power plant and chemical recovery systems.
- Environmental regulation and compliance — Strict pollution and water-usage rules require consistent, ongoing compliance investment in effluent treatment, afforestation and resource-saving practices.
- Technology obsolescence — Outdated machinery may not align with evolving global standards, risking operational inefficiency; the Company is modernising infrastructure and digitalising operations through Project Nirmaan to address this.
- Currency and interest-rate exposure — International trade exposes the Company to exchange-rate fluctuations (managed via hedging), while higher interest rates can escalate borrowing costs and reduce profitability.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Described as "a leading agro and wood-based paper manufacturer" that started commercial operations in 1980 "in an economically backward village of Hoshiarpur, Punjab", with a fully integrated manufacturing facility "spread across 259 acres".
- Claims the "Largest product portfolio in the Paper Industry covering Maplitho, Copier, Specialty and Creamwove papers" and says "Superior product quality and market focus allow us to charge premium price of 5-7% higher than competitors".
- "Located near densely populated Northern Region including NCR, a higher paper consumption market"; "Strategic location in Punjab with abundant availability of raw materials such as Wheat Straw, Sarkanda & Bagasse, allows us to get steady supplies at stable prices".
- Order-based manufacturing through a dealer network the deck sizes two ways: "120+ dealer network spread across India, many of whom have been associated with it for three generations" (About slide) versus "Pan India presence with an extensive network of 100+ dealers" and "many associated with the company for over 3 decades" (Key Strengths slide).
- Exports "to 26 countries"; marquee clients listed include Macmillan Education India, McGraw Hill Education India, Oxford University Press, Pearson India Education Services, HT Media, Rachna Sagar, Chitra Prakashan India, Magic International, SBM Industries and Today Diaries.

- [Capital market] Price Data (30th June, 2026): Face Value INR 1.0; Market Price 75.7; 52 Week H/L 134.3/65.5; Market Cap INR 6,601.5 Mn; Equity Shares Outstanding 87.3 Mn; 1 Year Avg Trading Volume 73.4 ('000). Share-price chart shows Kuantum against BSE Sensex from Jul-25 to Jun-26.

business.body: Kuantum Papers Limited, established in 1980 at Saila Khurd, District Hoshiarpur, Punjab, is a fully backward-integrated paper manufacturer spanning agro and wood pulping, co-generation power and chemical recovery systems across a 259-acre plant. It manufactures maplitho, copier, creamwove and specialty papers (thermal, bond, azurelaid, coloured and cartridge, plus sustainable cupstock, straw-based and carry-bag paper) and sells through a network of 120+ dealers pan-India together with a growing export footprint, serving education, printing & publishing, corporate and e-commerce customers.

outlook.body:
- Continue the Rs. 735 crore Mill Expansion and Upgradation Programme — modernising all four paper machines, augmenting wood pulping infrastructure (DDS), reinforcing utility systems and deploying advanced automation/AI — to raise paper production capacity from 450 TPD to 675 TPD
- Expand participation in premium, specialty and value-added paper segments rather than competing solely on scale or price, backed by R&D (e.g. Oil & Grease Resistant paper, Kuantum Korra, Kuantum Kopio)
- Accelerate digital transformation via Project Neev (digital foundation/connectivity) and Project Nirmaan (AI, IoT, Advanced Process Control, predictive analytics), with the AI-driven MACS/APC framework to be extended to Paper Machine 4 in the next year
- Leverage the established dealer network and product diversity across Maplitho, Creamwove, Copier and Specialty papers to deepen market relevance and respond to evolving customer requirements
- Embed sustainability across the value chain — Social Farm Forestry programme for future wood raw-material security, water reuse, energy efficiency, waste reduction and circularity
- Invest in people through leadership development and technical/skill-building programmes in automation, Advanced Process Control, predictive maintenance and Industry 4.0
- The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 3(2) of SEBI LODR (voluntarily, as it is not among the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation as at 31 December 2025 / 31 March 2026, the threshold at which such a policy is mandatory under Regulation 43A). The Directors' annual dividend recommendation is linked to the satisfactoriness of that year's business operations, i.e. dividend is treated as a payout tied to operating performance rather than a fixed formula.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Kuantum is executing a Rs. 735 crore Mill Upgradation & Expansion Project (commenced 2024) intended to raise installed paper production capacity from 450 TPD to 675 TPD and lift production volume from over 160,000 tonnes to more than 200,000 tonnes per annum. The programme covers modernisation of all four paper machines, new converting and offline coating facilities (entry into coated/flexible-packaging-base and other specialty segments), a Displacement Digester System (DDS) in the hardwood pulp line, upgraded Twin Roll Presses and chip-washing systems on both agro and wood pulp mills, a modernised recovery boiler with a new lime kiln, power-plant turbine/fuel-system upgrades, a canal-based water supply pipeline and Water Treatment Plant, and Effluent Treatment Plant upgrades. During FY26 the Company commissioned the upgraded PM4 (new shoe press, modified hood, oil-heated calender, upgraded drying systems), rebuilt PM1 (capacity raised to over 80 TPD) and PM2 (capacity raised to 75 TPD), upgraded the on-site PCC plant from 25,000 TPA to 50,000 TPA, retrofitted the 200 TPD Recovery Boiler (Two-Stage Causticizer, new Electrostatic Precipitator, cascade-to-economiser upgrade), progressed the Displacement Digester System and received regulatory approval to raise paper production capacity from 450 TPD to 540 TPD. The overall programme is expected to be completed in all respects by 30 September 2026, except the Offline Coater Plant which may extend to 31 March 2027.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government's National Education Policy (NEP 2020) and rising education spend expected to sharply increase demand for printing & writing paper (notebooks, textbooks, including 22-language NCERT textbooks)
- Nationwide ban on single-use plastics (effective July 2022) continuing to boost demand for paper-based substitutes such as cupstock, straw-base and carry-bag paper
- Growing e-commerce, FMCG, pharma and healthcare packaging demand, and the shift from plastic to paper-based packaging, expected to support Writing & Printing and specialty/packaging paper segments
- India's low per-capita paper consumption (15-16 kg vs global average of 57 kg) seen as significant structural headroom for demand growth
- FY26 saw a downtrend in the domestic paper industry — realisations fell (Kuantum's Net Sales Realisation declined ~3-4%) due to an oversupplied market from a surge in low-priced imports (particularly China and ASEAN), while input costs (domestic wood, agro residue, chemicals) rose due to constrained supply, floods in Punjab, competing demand from other wood-based industries, and the 2026 US-Israel/Iran conflict's impact on oil and chemical prices
- Management expects a rebound aided by NEP-driven Writing & Printing Paper (WPP) demand and increasing penetration of specialised and conventional packaging in FMCG, healthcare, e-commerce and pharmaceuticals
- Volatile raw material (wood, pulp) and energy prices remain a persistent margin driver, prompting continued investment in in-house pulping and alternative raw materials
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
